rows: The firmware shall target the STM32-NUCLEO-G070RB development board.
The firmware project shall provide a configurable LOGO_DISPLAY_MS macro in config.h with a default value of 2000.
The firmware project shall define the climate and ride-event thresholds, sudden window, and event display time as configurable parameters in config.h.
The firmware shall use 32 degC as the configured high-temperature threshold.
The firmware shall use 75% as the configured high-humidity threshold.
The firmware shall acquire temperature and humidity from a DHT22 sensor connected through PB4.
configs module, drivers/dht22 module, platforms/stm32 module, services module
The firmware shall interface with an MPU6050 3-axis accelerometer and gyroscope over I2C on PB8 (SCL) and PB9 (SDA), sharing the bus with the OLED.
configs module, interfaces module, platforms/stm32 module
The firmware shall coordinate access to the shared I2C bus so transactions to the MPU6050 and OLED do not overlap or corrupt one another.
configs module, interfaces module, platforms/stm32 module
While displaying the logo, the firmware shall initialize the DHT22 and perform MPU6050 zeroing in the background without extending the splash duration.
The firmware shall read temperature in degrees Celsius and humidity in percent from the DHT22 every 2 seconds.
configs module, drivers/dht22 module, platforms/stm32 module, services module
The firmware shall read the MPU6050 X, Y, and Z acceleration at 100 Hz using the +/-4 g range and convert the readings to g units.
app module, drivers/mpu6050 module, services module
At power-up, the firmware shall zero the MPU6050 readings after the board has been flat and still for 1 second, producing X = 0 g, Y = 0 g, and Z = 1 g.
app module, drivers/mpu6050 module, services module
The firmware shall map X acceleration to lateral cornering, Y acceleration to longitudinal acceleration/braking, and Z acceleration to vertical bumps.
app module, drivers/mpu6050 module, services module
The firmware shall detect failed DHT22 or MPU6050 acquisitions and shall not use failed acquisition results as valid displayed measurements or inputs to event detection.
app module, drivers/mpu6050 module, services module
The firmware shall drive a 1.3-inch I2C OLED using the SH1106 driver over PB8 (SCL) and PB9 (SDA), shared with the MPU6050.
drivers/sh1106 module, platforms/stm32 module, services module

The firmware project shall contain the CraftifAI logo as a flash-resident 1-bit monochrome bitmap array in logo.h, formatted for the SH1106 as 128x64 pixels, 8 pages by 128 columns, with LSB as the top row.
The firmware shall display the 124x26-pixel logo artwork centred on the display with a black border, white on a black background.
The firmware shall implement splash timing non-blockingly using HAL_GetTick rather than a blocking delay.
app module, platforms/stm32 module, services module
During the logo splash, the firmware shall show no alerts and shall not blink the LED.
app module, platforms/stm32 module, services module
The SH1106 driver shall apply a 2-column offset when writing the logo and all other screens to account for its 132 columns of RAM and 128 visible columns.
drivers/sh1106 module, platforms/stm32 module, services module
When an event occurs, the firmware shall immediately show its message on the OLED while keeping Temperature and Humidity visible.
After the splash, the firmware shall display a Vehicle Parameters screen containing temperature from the DHT22 in degC, humidity from the DHT22 in percent, and X, Y, and Z acceleration values in g.
The firmware shall initialize the SH1106 display interface before its first display write, early enough for the logo to appear within 100 ms of power-up.
app module, platforms/stm32 module, services module
On power-up or reset, the firmware shall display the CraftifAI logo on the OLED for 2 seconds before displaying sensor data or a heading, then switch to the Vehicle Parameters screen.
app module, platforms/stm32 module, services module
The firmware shall display the acceleration values on the Vehicle Parameters screen using the labels "X:", "Y:", and "Z:", with the Z value followed by " g".
When temperature or humidity exceeds its configured high limit, the firmware shall display an exclamation mark next to the corresponding value.
The firmware shall detect an event when its associated axis changes by at least the configured threshold within 100 ms.
app module, configs module, modules module

The firmware shall detect and identify Unseen SpeedBreaker when Z changes by at least 0.30 g, Wide Turn when X changes by at least 0.25 g, Speeding when Y changes positively by at least 0.25 g, and Sudden Braking when Y changes negatively by at least 0.25 g.
app module, configs module, modules module
The firmware shall control the inbuilt user LED LD4 through PA5.
app module, bsp module, modules module, platforms/stm32 module
While an event alert is active, the firmware shall blink LD4 at 1 Hz with 500 ms on and 500 ms off.
app module, bsp module, modules module, platforms/stm32 module
The firmware shall continue displaying the event message and blinking the LED for 2 seconds after the last event.
app module, bsp module, modules module, platforms/stm32 module
When event messages overlap, the firmware shall prioritize them in this order: Sudden Braking, Unseen SpeedBreaker, Wide Turn, then Speeding.
app module, configs module, modules module
The firmware shall stream cabin comfort and ride data to a dashboard for driver-behaviour review or ride-comfort tracking.

figures.caption: Normal acquisition, processing and output sequence.
figures.mermaid:
sequenceDiagram
  participant Main as STM32 main
  participant App as app_start
  participant IO as platform_io
  participant Sensors as Sensor service
  participant I2C as I2C1 devices
  participant Ride as Ride event module
  participant Display as Display service
  participant Telemetry as Telemetry services
  participant UART as USART2 console

  Main->>App: app_start
  App->>Telemetry: firmgen_telemetry_start
  App->>IO: platform_io_init
  alt I/O initialization fails
    IO-->>App: false
    App-->>Main: return
  else I/O initialization succeeds
    IO-->>App: true
    App->>IO: platform_io_scan
    IO->>I2C: scan device addresses
    IO->>UART: log bus scan results
    App->>Display: display_init
    Display->>I2C: initialize and clear SH1106
    App->>Sensors: sensors_init
    Sensors->>I2C: initialize MPU6050 at 0x68
    App->>Ride: ride_events_init
    loop app_start cooperative loop
      App->>Telemetry: firmgen_telemetry_poll
      App->>IO: platform_io_now_ms and platform_io_poll
      App->>Sensors: sensors_process
      Sensors->>I2C: scheduled MPU6050 reads
      Sensors->>IO: scheduled DHT22 frame read on PB4
      App->>Sensors: sensors_snapshot
      alt Display ready and splash finished
        alt Acceleration is valid
          App->>Ride: ride_events_sample with acceleration
        else Acceleration is invalid
          App->>Ride: ride_events_sample with NULL
        end
        App->>Ride: ride_events_update
      end
      opt Ride event changed
        App->>Display: display_set_event
        App->>IO: log event change
      end
      App->>IO: platform_io_led
      opt LED state changed
        App->>IO: log LED command
      end
      opt Display initialized
        App->>Display: display_process with readings
        Display->>I2C: update display pages when due
      end
      App->>Telemetry: telemetry_process
      Telemetry->>IO: queue CSV record when due
      IO->>UART: transmit queued bytes
      Telemetry->>UART: send boot/runtime telemetry when due
    end
  end
